text.p: Tropical Cyclone 07B is moving westward across the Bay of Bengal and is expected to have top winds near 80 mph at the time of landfall in about 12-18 hours, which will occur near Vajayavada and Guntur, India. Heavy rain will likely lead to flash-flooding. Wind damage is also likely, especially near the coast. Coastal flooding will result from a strong coastal storm surge. The storm will then move inland and weaken rapidly but will likely produce heavy showers and local flooding into south central India.

Tropical Cyclone Melanie-Bellamine is a very powerful storm with 120 mph top winds. The storm threatens only shipping in the southern Indian Ocean. It is centered near 11s/82e and tracking to the west southwest. It is expected to pick up foward speed and graudally weaken over the next 48 hours.

Tropical storm Dale remains well southeast of Guam. It is expected to strengthen during the next 24-48 hours, becoming an increasing risk to shipping. Dale may be a minimal typhoon when it approaches Guam by 36-48 hours. Further strengthening is possible as it moves to the west.

Tropical Depression 37W is making landfall over the southern Philippine island of Mindanao. Top winds are near 35 mph. Locally heavy rains and gusty winds will continue for the next 6-12 hours before the storm crosses over into the South China Sea and re-intensifies. This system will become an increasing risk to shipping in the south South China Sea at that time.
